Subject: Packaging question — consolidation vs feature-first + fallback credits?

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're evaluating Redwood for a set of mixed workloads (inference-heavy triage + lower-latency chat features). Before we progress with procurement I need clarity on packaging:

- If we go with the Consolidated Throughput plan (fewer features, higher burst), what is the downgrade path after the pilot? Specifically, can we step down without losing access to customer-facing features for a defined window?
- If we go feature-first (per-feature entitlements), what is the uplift in unit cost and are there credits available to mitigate the migration risk?
- We asked about a short-term fallback/flex credit (in case we need to revert after production). How long do credits last and what constraints apply?

Procurement asked for a sample quote and SOW we can attach to the contract. Can you share an updated quote that shows: normal list price vs 12-month commit discount vs a pilot concession (credits)? Also, any language around a rollback or canary window would help.

Appreciate a clear, compact proposal. Timing: procurement wants something they can review by Friday 6/13.

Best,
Bethany
Head of Product Operations
Lucent Health

Subject: Re: Packaging question — consolidation vs feature-first + fallback credits?

Hi Bethany — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then a compact proposal.

TL;DR
- Consolidated Throughput: best unit economics for inference-heavy workloads; safe downgrade path but with a 30-day window where we preserve feature flags and exports.
- Feature-first: more granular control and faster rollbacks for specific features, ~12–18% higher per-unit cost in our standard pricing; we can offer pilot credits to offset migration risk.
- Fallback credits: 90-day expiry, usable against token/throughput charges and reserved bursts; cannot be converted to cash.

Proposal (two viable options)
1) Throughput-First (recommended for triage workload)
   - 6-month pilot period: Reserved throughput slab with burst pool.
   - Pilot concession: $25k in fallback credits (applied to token/throughput charges), expires 90 days after invoice.
   - Downgrade path: we allow a one-time step-down within the pilot + a 30-day preservation window for feature flags and export access.
   - Discount: 8% off list with 12-month commit (applies if you convert pilot to annual).

2) Feature-First (recommended if feature isolation is critical)
   - Per-feature entitlements with seat/throughput mix.
   - Pilot concession: $15k in fallback credits, expires 90 days.
   - Downgrade path: per-feature rollback immediate; entitlements can be toggled with no data loss, but throughput will be billed at feature-first rates.
   - Discount: 10% off list with 12-month commit (higher discount to offset higher per-unit cost).

Operational notes
- Credits: usable for any Redwood billing line (tokens, reserved throughput, burst). They cannot be applied to third-party cloud egress or marketplace fees.
- Canary / rollback: we document a 2-week canary period in the SOW where Redwood will support a rollback and provide one-time export assistance (logs, KV cache snapshots).
- SOW/Quote: attaching a revised quote and SOW draft for procurement (lucent_quote_v2.pdf, SOW-draft-8472.docx). These show list vs commit pricing and the pilot concession line.

Next steps
- If you can confirm which option you prefer we will prepare a final commercial with a 12-month commit path (if you want the 10%/8% discount).
- If procurement needs different credit expiry or additional canary language we can loop legal; both concessions are negotiable within reason.

Thanks — looping Aditya (infrastructure) for any technical constraints on the canary/rollback side.

—Mateo

Hi Bethany — looping in a short technical and commercial clarification from infra/sales-engineering side.

Credit expiry: we can make the 90-day window start from activation date (not invoice). That means credits begin when you turn the pilot on and last 90 days thereafter. We'll reflect this change in the SOW.

Export assistance: Redwood will provide:
- A one-time KV cache snapshot (tar.gz of model keys + prefix cache) up to 20GB;
- Structured request/response logs in JSONL (compressed) covering the canary window;
- Guidance for replaying requests on your side.
Note: for very large exports we may need a short-runbook scheduling call to stage the transfer.

Short-term discount: Sales is authorized to add a one-time 5% contract credit (applied to first invoice) to help with SOW/procurement costs.

Rollback buffer: we'll include a 2-week rollback assistance window in the SOW (as Mateo suggested). During that time Redwood will:
- Keep feature flags live for your account if you request rollback;
- Provide export assistance and priority CS support;
- Offer a one-time migration carry-forward: up to 20% of unused pilot credits can be applied to the first month post-conversion (subject to approval).
